title: GoodDiffusion: Proactive Copyright Protection for Diffusion Generative Models via Learnable Sample-specific Signatures
claim: Static, universal protections can be bypassed or fail to block misuse; sample-specific, learnable controls permit authorized use and force unauthorized users to a warning output.
layout: 2 stacked left panels plus large right landscape; trajectories flow left-to-right
description: The figure has two parts. On the left, two stacked rounded panels contrast a gray 'Static Signature' (white-box vulnerable) with a green 'Sample-Specific Signatures' (white-box robust). The static panel shows a fixed pixel-grid key, an attacker's optimization loop, and a bypass image. The sample-specific panel shows three input images going through a neural 'LSN' network, which outputs a different signature pattern for each input. A hacker icon is crossed out, and the label reads 'No Universal Surrogate'. On the right, a large tilted terrain slab shades from blue to red, with generation time running along its bottom edge. Original inputs, authorized inputs and target images sit on distribution peaks. A gray arrow for standard I2I diffusion and a pink arrow for watermarking both reach the target. A bold blue arrow for the authorized GoodDiffusion path also reaches it. A red arrow for the unauthorized path ends at a warning-image spike. Callout boxes in purple, blue and red state the message, with a red ✗ and a green ✓ beside them.
caption: Overview of GoodDiffusion. (Left) The static signature design is vulnerable in white-box scenarios, while the sample-specific signature design can effectively defend against malicious model thieves. (Right) The trained DBM integrates two diffusion bridges. The authorized trajectory (blue) follows pauth(˜x1) →pauth(x0 | ˜x1). The unauthorized trajectory (red) follows pwarn(x1) →pwarn(¯x0). Although watermarks can be used for passive protection, the gap between watermarked and non-watermarked images may be imperceptible to human eyes, thus still allowing unauthorized usage. However, GoodDiffusion provides early proactive control: the unauthorized user can only generate the warning image, which is completely different from the target images.
abstract: This paper tackles the challenging problem of developing a proactive copyright protection mechanism that cuts off unauthorized use of diffusion bridge models. Existing studies largely fall into post-hoc attribution (e.g., watermarking and fingerprinting) or degradation-only defenses, which offer only indirect and limited preventive effects. We therefore propose GoodDiffusion, inspired by backdoor mechanisms, to enforce model-level use-time control by internalizing authorization into the generative process through a selectively permissive, otherwise closed behavior. Specifically, GoodDiffusion preserves high-quality generation for authorized queries carrying valid signatures, yet refuses to generate for unauthorized inputs. We further theoretically show that naive static-signature designs (like conventional backdoor injection) are fundamentally fragile, since a surrogate signature can be efficiently recovered via gradient-based optimization. To strengthen security, we introduce a Learnable Signature Network (LSN) that assigns sample-specific signatures conditioned on each input. This breaks the universality of signatures and prevents a surrogate from transferring across inputs. Extensive experiments validate that GoodDiffusion effectively blocks unauthorized use while maintaining strong generation quality for authorized users.
